title: Transfer Case Control System (MIL Request)
shortDescription: Transfer case controller has requested MIL illumination.
fullDescription:
P0800 is set by the PCM when the transfer case control module reports a fault. It is a generic 'see sub-codes' indicator on 4WD/AWD vehicles.

Retrieve TCCM-specific DTCs to identify the actual issue (encoder motor, mode switch, or actuator).

faq.a: Usually yes — but get the sub-code addressed.

title: Transmission Control System MIL Request Circuit Open
shortDescription: TCM-to-PCM MIL request line is open.
fullDescription:
P0802 sets when the dedicated MIL-request signal between the TCM and PCM is open-circuit. The PCM cannot tell whether the TCM is requesting MIL.

Usually a wiring break or connector issue.
safetyImpact: Possible delayed MIL warning of transmission issues.

fixSteps.title: Continuity test
fixSteps.instruction: Check wire from TCM to PCM.

faq.a: Rodent damage or chafed wiring.

title: 1-4 Upshift Solenoid Circuit
fullDescription:
P0803 indicates the 1-4 upshift (skip-shift) solenoid circuit has an electrical fault. The skip-shift system forces a 1-to-4 shift on light-throttle to improve fuel economy on certain manual GM vehicles.

Fix is usually solenoid replacement or wiring repair.
safetyImpact: No driveability issues; CAGS feature inoperative.

faq.a: Aftermarket eliminators exist; stock fix is solenoid replacement.

title: 1-4 Upshift Lamp Circuit
fullDescription: P0804 sets when the 1-4 upshift indicator lamp circuit malfunctions on manual transmission vehicles equipped with CAGS. The bulb, socket, or wiring is at fault.

faq.a: None — purely an indicator code.

title: Clutch Position Sensor Range/Performance
fullDescription:
P0806 sets when the clutch position sensor on a manual or automated-manual transmission produces an implausible signal — out of expected range for current pedal travel.

Likely sensor failure or misalignment.

faq.a: Manual or automated manual transmissions.

title: Clutch Position Sensor Circuit Low
fullDescription:
P0807 indicates the clutch position sensor signal is below the expected lower threshold — short to ground or sensor failure.

Diagnose wiring before replacing sensor.

faq.a: Not recommended — affects safety interlocks.

title: Clutch Position Sensor Circuit High
fullDescription:
P0808 sets when the clutch position sensor signal exceeds expected high threshold — short to voltage or open ground.

Check wiring carefully before condemning the sensor.
safetyImpact: Cruise and start may be disabled.

faq.a: Opposite polarity — high vs low.

title: Excessive Clutch Slippage
fullDescription:
P0811 sets when input speed greatly exceeds vehicle speed for the engaged manual gear, indicating clutch slip. Contaminated, worn, or oil-soaked clutch friction surfaces are typical.

Driving with this code accelerates clutch failure.

fixSteps.title: Verify slip
fixSteps.instruction: Drive in high gear, accelerate, watch RPM/MPH.

fixSteps.title: Inspect rear main
fixSteps.instruction: Check for oil leak contaminating clutch.

fixSteps.title: Replace clutch
fixSteps.instruction: Install new clutch kit and resurface flywheel.

faq.a: No — clutch must be replaced.

title: Reverse Input Circuit
fullDescription:
P0813 sets when the reverse switch or PRNDL reverse position input is electrically faulty. Reverse lights and rear-camera triggers may also be affected.

Diagnose with a multimeter at the switch.
safetyImpact: Reverse lamps may not work — visibility hazard at night.

faq.a: Yes, but reverse lights may be out.

title: Transmission Range Display Circuit
fullDescription: P0814 indicates the gear range display in the cluster is not receiving a valid signal. Cluster bulbs, PRNDL switch, or wiring are typical sources.
safetyImpact: Driver may not see gear position.

faq.a: Yes — but display may be missing.

title: Up and Down Shift Switch to Transmission Range Correlation
shortDescription: Tiptronic shift inputs disagree with PRNDL.
fullDescription:
P0819 sets when manual shift mode (Tiptronic / Sport) up/down inputs do not correlate with the actual transmission range sensor reading.

Likely a faulty paddle/console switch or wiring fault.

fixSteps.title: Switch test
fixSteps.instruction: Check up/down inputs in scan tool.

fixSteps.title: Replace switch
fixSteps.instruction: Swap shifter assembly or paddle module.

faq.a: Usually yes — only manual mode is affected.

title: Gear Lever X-Y Position Circuit
fullDescription:
P0821 sets on electronic shift-by-wire systems when the X-Y position sensor of the gear lever circuit is faulty. The TCM can no longer determine selector position.

Usually requires shifter module replacement.

faq.a: Modern shift-by-wire — VW/Audi, BMW, Jaguar.

title: Gear Lever Y Position Circuit
fullDescription: P0822 indicates the Y-axis (typically up/down) hall sensor on the shift lever has an electrical fault. Diagnosis mirrors P0821.

fixSteps.title: Scan live
fixSteps.instruction: Watch X/Y data while moving lever.

faq.a: Usually module replacement — sensors are integrated.

title: Gear Lever X Position Circuit Intermittent
fullDescription:
P0823 sets when the X-axis shifter sensor signal is intermittent. The TCM occasionally loses track of selector position.

Look for connector seating or solder joint failures inside the shift module.

fixSteps.title: Wiggle test
fixSteps.instruction: Move lever while monitoring scan tool.

faq.a: Marginal — shifter glitches can leave you in wrong gear.

title: Gear Lever Y Position Circuit Intermittent
fullDescription:
P0824 indicates the Y-axis sensor of the gear lever produces intermittent readings. Counterpart to P0823.

Usually a shift module hardware issue.

faq.a: Some manufacturers issue firmware updates — check TSBs.

title: Up and Down Shift Switch Circuit Low
fullDescription:
P0827 sets when the up/down (Tiptronic) switch input is stuck low — short to ground or a stuck-closed switch.

Replace switch or repair wiring.

faq.a: Yes — only manual mode is affected.

title: Up and Down Shift Switch Circuit High
fullDescription:
P0828 sets when the manual up/down switch input is stuck high — short to voltage or open ground.

Diagnose wiring before replacing the switch.

faq.a: Opposite polarity.

title: 5-6 Shift Malfunction
fullDescription:
P0829 sets when the TCM detects a problem during the 5-6 shift event — slip, late shift, or solenoid issue.

Diagnose with ratio data and solenoid command tests.

faq.a: Possible short term — but expect higher fuel use.

title: Reverse Inhibit Control Circuit
fullDescription:
P0801 sets when the reverse-inhibit solenoid (prevents engaging R while moving forward) circuit is faulty.

Replace solenoid or repair wiring.

faq.a: Yes — but be careful when selecting reverse.

title: Clutch Position Sensor Circuit
fullDescription:
P0805 sets when the clutch position sensor circuit has a generic fault — open, short, or unstable signal.

Diagnose wiring and sensor; replace as required.

faq.a: Different — P0805 is the position sensor electrical circuit.

title: Clutch Position Control Error
fullDescription: P0810 sets on dual-clutch and automated-manual gearboxes when actual clutch position deviates from commanded for too long. Worn clutch, leaking actuator, or air in hydraulics are common.

faq.a: Mostly — and automated manuals.

title: Upshift Switch Circuit
fullDescription:
P0815 indicates the upshift portion of the manual-mode switch has an electrical fault. Driver cannot upshift in manual mode.

Replace switch or repair wiring.

faq.a: Yes — only manual upshift affected.

title: Gear Lever X-Y Position Sensor Correlation
shortDescription: X and Y lever sensors disagree.
fullDescription:
P0820 sets when the X and Y position sensors of the gear lever produce values that don't correlate. One sensor may be drifting.

Usually requires shifter module replacement.

faq.a: Some platforms allow it; others need new module.

title: Clutch Actuator Circuit Open
fullDescription:
P0900 in this generic context indicates the clutch actuator control circuit is open. Found mostly on dual-clutch automatics. The TCM cannot energize the actuator.

Wiring or actuator failure.

faq.a: Often yes if no-drive.

title: Clutch Actuator Circuit High
fullDescription:
P0902 indicates the clutch actuator control circuit is reading high. Short to voltage or open ground are likely.

Diagnose with multimeter; repair wiring or replace actuator.

faq.a: Wiring possibly; actuator usually pro.

title: Gear Shift Forward Actuator Circuit Range/Performance
fullDescription:
P0925 indicates the forward shift actuator (electronic) does not move as commanded within the expected response window. Common on automated-manual transmissions.

Replace actuator or service hydraulics.

faq.a: Mostly automated manuals and DCTs.

title: Gear Shift Reverse Actuator Circuit
fullDescription:
P0930 sets when the reverse shift actuator electrical circuit is faulty — open or short. Vehicle may not engage reverse.

Replace actuator after wiring check.

faq.a: No — actuator must work to engage gears.

title: Hydraulic Pressure Sensor Circuit Malfunction
fullDescription:
P0940 sets when the transmission hydraulic pressure sensor reports an electrical fault. The TCM cannot regulate line pressure accurately.

Replace sensor after wiring check.
safetyImpact: Harsh shifts; potential damage if ignored.

faq.a: Yes — pan drop required.

title: Auto Shift Manual Adaptive Learning Malfunction
fullDescription:
P0950 sets when the TCM's adaptive learning (used to compensate for clutch wear) fails to converge. May indicate excessive clutch wear or sensor issues.

Fluid service and adaptation reset is the first step; rebuild may be required.

fixSteps.title: Reset adapts
fixSteps.instruction: Use scan tool to clear and relearn.

faq.a: Worth trying after fluid service.

title: Pressure Control Solenoid A Control Circuit Open
fullDescription:
P0960 sets when the TCM detects an open in the control circuit of pressure control solenoid A. Open wire, bad connector, or failed solenoid coil.

Diagnose with multimeter and replace as needed.

faq.a: Related — different DTC range, similar component.
